payload.title: [native-swift-4] Unbounded reserveCapacity from attacker-controlled array/map length header (memory DoS)
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING native-swift-4 (medium/dos, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: packages/swift/Sources/FrickSwift/FrickSyncSocket.swift
LINES: 496-514, 443-446

WHAT: `readArray`/`readMap` call `reserveCapacity(count)` where `count` comes directly from a 16-/32-bit length header (`0xDC..0xDF`) before any element is read or bounds-checked against remaining bytes. A frame declaring a 4-byte array length near UInt32.max (~4.29e9) triggers an immediate multi-gigabyte allocation attempt (`reserveCapacity` for `[FrickMsgPackValue]`) even though the body is truncated — the subsequent `decode` would throw `.truncated`, but the over-reservation happens first. The new call/removal frames widen the set of server-pushed payloads parsed this way.

IMPACT: A single small malicious frame forces a huge allocation, crashing the client with an out-of-memory abort. Remote DoS.

SUGGESTED FIX: Cap `count` against remaining bytes before reserving (each element is ≥1 byte, so `count` cannot exceed `data.count - cursor`); reject lengths that exceed the buffer, and clamp `reserveCapacity` to a sane bound.
